Status: full conceptual companion / proposed framework with explicit evidence boundaries
Date: 2026-10-02
Definition history: unchanged snapshots in foundations/01_world_explanation.md, foundations/02_scientific_framework.md, and foundations/03_mathematical_core.md. Current publication scope is set by README and this audited companion.
Purpose: capture the full source-direction mechanism developed in the 2026-10-02 session, including the simplest physical examples, the recursive hierarchy, the relation to life, effective laws, expansion, and the engineering implications — without rewriting the already locked RRG definitions.

Publication orientation — added in the 2026-10-02 audit
The immediate project is to explain, publish, catalogue evidence and invite contributions—not to require its author to prove universal physics first. Mathematics and experiments below are optional avenues for contributors. The long-form discussion is retained so the source mechanism, life comparison, expansion idea and engineering implications are not lost through over-compression.
The core remains R=(G,M)R=(G,M)R=(G,M), G↔MG\leftrightarrow MG↔M, and Bn→Rn→Bn+1B_n\to R_n\to B_{n+1}Bn​→Rn​→Bn+1​. The stronger possibility of one form-invariant equation family is an additional mathematical conjecture, not a new definition of the author’s idea. “Locked” means changes must be explicit and versioned; it does not mean empirically established.
Empirical examples are documented in 06 — Evidence catalogue. 05 is optional. 08 — Claim and session coverage preserves the full set of ideas and distinguishes them from current evidence. Sections 7, 8, 11, 13–14, 24–25 and 33–43 have explicit audit corrections. Earlier text is preserved in archive/.

0. Why this document exists
The previous RRG documents established the local closure:
R=(G,M)\boxed{R=(G,M)}R=(G,M)​
with:
G↔M\boxed{G\leftrightarrow M}G↔M​
where geometry determines the modes a system can support, and active modes act back on the geometry.
The missing conceptual layer was the source direction:

How can a new resonant geometry appear from a lower-level background, change that background, and thereby create the conditions from which another level can appear?

The central extension developed here is:
Bn→Rn→Bn+1→Rn+1→⋯\boxed{
B_n
\rightarrow
R_n
\rightarrow
B_{n+1}
\rightarrow
R_{n+1}
\rightarrow\cdots
}Bn​→Rn​→Bn+1​→Rn+1​→⋯​
where:

BnB_nBn​ is the effective background available at level nnn,
Rn=(Gn,Mn)R_n=(G_n,M_n)Rn​=(Gn​,Mn​) is a persistent resonant geometry emerging within it,
the existence of RnR_nRn​ transforms what later structures experience as their environment,
the transformed environment can support structures and modes that were not accessible before.

This document is intentionally broader than a mathematical addendum. It records the full conceptual chain, its strongest known physical analogues, the open claims, and the forward research program.

1. Lock boundary: existing RRG definitions remain unchanged
This document does not redefine the core primitives.
1.1 Geometry
G={components, positions, connectivity, order, orientation, boundaries, constraints}.G=
\{\text{components, positions, connectivity, order, orientation, boundaries, constraints}\}.G={components, positions, connectivity, order, orientation, boundaries, constraints}.
Geometry is relational organization, not merely visible Euclidean outline.
1.2 Mode
M={ω,ϕ,A,ψ(x),propagation,coupling,τ,…}.M=
\{\omega,\phi,A,\psi(x),\text{propagation},\text{coupling},\tau,\ldots\}.M={ω,ϕ,A,ψ(x),propagation,coupling,τ,…}.
In intuitive discussion we often say frequency, but the scientific object is the full mode structure: frequency or spectrum, phase, amplitude, spatial pattern, coupling, propagation, and characteristic times.
A mode can be spatial, temporal or both. A stationary pattern is not automatically a temporal resonator. When a paper supplies only a spatial eigenmode or a steady attractor, the catalogue records that narrower result rather than silently treating it as proof of resonant self-maintenance.
1.3 Resonant dynamic geometry
R=(G,M)\boxed{R=(G,M)}R=(G,M)​
1.4 Dynamic closure / persistence
G→M→G\boxed{G\rightarrow M\rightarrow G}G→M→G​
A resonant geometry is persistent when its geometry supports a compatible mode structure and those dynamics maintain, restore, or continually recreate the organized state.
1.5 Scale
A scale is an effective regime in which a lower-level persistent structure can be treated as an effective unit by the next description level.
This document adds the explicit recursive background object BnB_nBn​ and makes the source-direction loop central.

2. Rule 0 — the source-direction statement
The candidate source rule is:

In an active background, transient geometries continuously appear. A geometry that supports a mode which reinforces or reconstructs that geometry can persist as a resonant dynamic structure. Persistent resonant structures then become part of the background and boundary conditions from which subsequent structures emerge.

In compact form:
Bn→Gn↔Mn→Rn→Bn+1\boxed{
B_n
\rightarrow
G_n
\leftrightarrow
M_n
\rightarrow
R_n
\rightarrow
B_{n+1}
}Bn​→Gn​↔Mn​→Rn​→Bn+1​​
and therefore:
B0→R0→B1→R1→B2→R2→⋯\boxed{
B_0
\rightarrow
R_0
\rightarrow
B_1
\rightarrow
R_1
\rightarrow
B_2
\rightarrow
R_2
\rightarrow\cdots
}B0​→R0​→B1​→R1​→B2​→R2​→⋯​
This is the current candidate Recursive Background Generator.
The important claim is not that every level looks the same. The claim is that the same abstract operation can run in different inherited backgrounds.

3. Level 0: begin from activity, not from pre-built resonators
The source model should not begin by assuming a universe already full of completed resonators.
Begin instead with the lowest effective background available to the theory:
B0.\boxed{B_0}.B0​​.
Intuitively, this can be imagined as a fluctuating or noise-like background.
However, RRG does not yet claim that the physical primordial universe was mathematically ideal white noise. White noise has a precise meaning: a flat spectrum with very short correlations. The correct scientific term is therefore:
effective fluctuating background\boxed{\text{effective fluctuating background}}effective fluctuating background​
or, when the approximation is justified:
effective noise bath.\boxed{\text{effective noise bath}}.effective noise bath​.
The conceptual starting point is simply that B0B_0B0​ contains dynamics before any higher persistent organization has been selected.
Transient configurations continually occur:
B0→{G0(1),G0(2),G0(3),…}.B_0
\rightarrow
\{G_0^{(1)},G_0^{(2)},G_0^{(3)},\ldots\}.B0​→{G0(1)​,G0(2)​,G0(3)​,…}.
Most are temporary.
But if one configuration supports a mode that acts back on the configuration in a stabilizing way:
G0(∗)→M0(∗)→G0(∗),G_0^{(*)}
\rightarrow
M_0^{(*)}
\rightarrow
G_0^{(*)},G0(∗)​→M0(∗)​→G0(∗)​,
then a closed loop has appeared:
R0=(G0(∗),M0(∗)).\boxed{R_0=(G_0^{(*)},M_0^{(*)})}.R0​=(G0(∗)​,M0(∗)​)​.
This is the first essential transition:
fluctuation→self-consistent resonant geometry→persistence\boxed{
\text{fluctuation}
\rightarrow
\text{self-consistent resonant geometry}
\rightarrow
\text{persistence}
}fluctuation→self-consistent resonant geometry→persistence​
No separate law saying "become an object" is needed if the dynamics themselves contain attractors or stable closed mode–geometry relationships.

4. The first persistent resonator changes what comes next
Before R0R_0R0​ existed, the surrounding background was B0B_0B0​.
After R0R_0R0​ exists, the environment is not identical anymore.
The resonator:

scatters and filters existing fluctuations,
introduces characteristic frequencies and phase relations,
changes local boundary conditions,
can store and release energy,
can alter propagation paths,
can couple previously weak degrees of freedom,
can suppress some modes and enhance others,
can create new spatial or temporal correlations.

Therefore:
(B0,R0)→B0′\boxed{
(B_0,R_0)
\rightarrow
B_0'
}(B0​,R0​)→B0′​​
and with many persistent level-0 structures:
B1=B(B0,{R0},their interactions/history)\boxed{
B_1
=
\mathcal B(B_0,\{R_0\},\text{their interactions/history})
}B1​=B(B0​,{R0​},their interactions/history)​
The first resonator therefore does not merely survive inside the background.
It becomes part of what defines the background experienced by later structures.
This is one of the central additions of v0.2.

5. Geometry creates mode; mode shapes geometry
The simplest local engine remains:
G→M→G′\boxed{
G\rightarrow M\rightarrow G'
}G→M→G′​
or, at closure:
G↔M.\boxed{
G\leftrightarrow M.
}G↔M.​
A familiar visible example is a vibrating plate covered in sand.
The plate geometry and boundary conditions determine allowed mechanical modes. The mode produces spatially nonuniform motion. Sand grains migrate and accumulate in characteristic regions, producing a visible pattern linked to the mode.
So we already know experimentally that:
mode / vibration→reorganization of matter→geometry\boxed{
\text{mode / vibration}
\rightarrow
\text{reorganization of matter}
\rightarrow
\text{geometry}
}mode / vibration→reorganization of matter→geometry​
can occur.
The RRG claim is not that sand patterns prove the whole theory.
Their importance is that they make one half of the mechanism directly visible: dynamics can select and impose spatial organization.
The opposite half is equally ordinary: changing the plate's geometry or boundaries changes its allowed vibration spectrum.
Thus the physically familiar pair is:
geometry determines modesandmodes can reorganize geometry/material\boxed{
\text{geometry determines modes}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\text{modes can reorganize geometry/material}
}geometry determines modesandmodes can reorganize geometry/material​
RRG asks how far this mutual relationship can be generalized.

6. Coupled resonators show that one mode can become collective
Another established piece is synchronization.
Coupled pendulums, metronomes, clocks, lasers, electrical oscillators, chemical oscillators, and biological rhythms can phase-lock or form collective modes under suitable coupling.
For mechanical metronomes on a movable platform:
{Ri}→shared platform motion→{Ri}\{R_i\}
\rightarrow
\text{shared platform motion}
\rightarrow
\{R_i\}{Ri​}→shared platform motion→{Ri​}
and a collective synchronized state can emerge.
The relevant principle is:
individual oscillators+coupling→collective resonant mode\boxed{
\text{individual oscillators}
+
\text{coupling}
\rightarrow
\text{collective resonant mode}
}individual oscillators+coupling→collective resonant mode​
This matters for the source model because it shows that larger collective modes do not need to be separately programmed. They can arise from interactions among smaller oscillatory units.
It also corrects an overly simple picture in which one oscillator "commands" all others. Often the shared environment is part of the loop:
R1,R2,…,RN→B→R1,R2,…,RN.R_1,R_2,\ldots,R_N
\rightarrow
B
\rightarrow
R_1,R_2,\ldots,R_N.R1​,R2​,…,RN​→B→R1​,R2​,…,RN​.
The collective mode and the components mutually create one another's dynamical conditions.

7. Scale matching: why different levels respond to different modes
The session's scale intuition is important but must be stated carefully.
The useful principle is not:

smaller things are always influenced more strongly.

It is:

Different geometries and scales have different natural mode spectra, so they couple selectively to different spatial and temporal patterns.

In many simple resonators, a characteristic frequency scales schematically like:
f∼vL\boxed{
f\sim \frac{v}{L}
}f∼Lv​​
although the exact power law depends on the physical system, dimensions, stiffness, mass distribution, and boundary conditions.
This gives the common tendency:
smaller/faster structures↔higher characteristic frequencies\boxed{
\text{smaller/faster structures}
\leftrightarrow
\text{higher characteristic frequencies}
}smaller/faster structures↔higher characteristic frequencies​
and:
larger collective structures↔slower collective modes\boxed{
\text{larger collective structures}
\leftrightarrow
\text{slower collective modes}
}larger collective structures↔slower collective modes​
without claiming this as a universal one-line law for every system.
The earthquake/building example from the conversation illustrates the intended intuition; it is not a measured universal scale law. At smaller scales, the verified microparticle experiment in 06, E03 demonstrates acoustic manipulation. That source supports micrometre particles, not every nano-to-cosmic scale. A size comparison must hold material properties and boundary conditions sufficiently comparable; different classes of resonators can have different scaling. These observations motivate the hierarchy idea without establishing it.
So the deeper point is:
a mode strongly reorganizes degrees of freedom that can couple to that mode\boxed{
\text{a mode strongly reorganizes degrees of freedom that can couple to that mode}
}a mode strongly reorganizes degrees of freedom that can couple to that mode​
not "sound only affects sand" or "small things require sound".
At molecular, electronic, nuclear, or quantum scales, the relevant mode and coupling channels can be completely different.

8. Time and persistence matter because influence can accumulate
A transient fluctuation can have only a brief effect.
A persistent resonator can interact with its environment through many cycles. Repetition does not guarantee indefinite energy accumulation: losses, saturation and thresholds can prevent any lasting reorganization. A long lifetime and a long phase-coherence time are also different quantities.
Let:

τR\tau_RτR​ = resonator lifetime,
TRT_RTR​ = characteristic period,
NR∼τR/TRN_R\sim \tau_R/T_RNR​∼τR​/TR​ = approximate number of cycles during the lifetime (not necessarily phase-coherent cycles),
CRC_RCR​ = effective coupling to surrounding degrees of freedom.

Then a longer-lived, well-coupled resonator has more opportunities to produce cumulative changes.
The qualitative principle is:
persistence×coupling×available interaction time→historical influence\boxed{
\text{persistence}
\times
\text{coupling}
\times
\text{available interaction time}
\rightarrow
\text{historical influence}
}persistence×coupling×available interaction time→historical influence​
This does not mean that the most stable object always dominates.
A highly stable object may couple almost not at all to its surroundings. A strongly coupled state may destroy itself. A mode may have no compatible substrate on which to act.
The scientifically defensible statement is:

Persistence increases the opportunity for environmental influence when a suitable coupling and conversion pathway exist.


9. Expansion does not need to be a separate command
A central insight from the session is that "expand" need not be written as an independent law.
Suppose a persistent geometry GGG supports a mode MMM:
G→M.G\rightarrow M.G→M.
Suppose that mode acts on nearby compatible degrees of freedom and makes more geometry compatible with GGG:
M+background→G+.M+\text{background}
\rightarrow
G^+.M+background→G+.
If the new geometry supports the same or a compatible mode:
G+ightarrowM+,G^+
ightarrow M^+,G+ightarrowM+,
then the loop can propagate:
G→M→G+→M+→G++→⋯\boxed{
G
\rightarrow
M
\rightarrow
G^+
\rightarrow
M^+
\rightarrow
G^{++}
\rightarrow\cdots
}G→M→G+→M+→G++→⋯​
This is expansion by positive feedback, not because the structure contains an abstract goal to grow.
Required ingredients remain physical:
compatible structure+coupling+available energy/flux when required+accessible substrate\boxed{
\text{compatible structure}
+
\text{coupling}
+
\text{available energy/flux when required}
+
\text{accessible substrate}
}compatible structure+coupling+available energy/flux when required+accessible substrate​
If losses exceed reinforcement, the expansion stops.
If another incompatible stable domain competes for the same degrees of freedom, boundaries or competition can appear.
If several modes are mutually compatible or use different resources, coexistence is possible.
Therefore the framework does not assume:
one resonance must conquer everything.\text{one resonance must conquer everything}.one resonance must conquer everything.
It predicts a spectrum of possibilities:
decay, persistence, expansion, coexistence, competition, transformation\boxed{
\text{decay, persistence, expansion, coexistence, competition, transformation}
}decay, persistence, expansion, coexistence, competition, transformation​
depending on the actual dynamics.

10. Selection can emerge without a special selection law
Once multiple persistent structures are possible, differential persistence follows automatically.
Consider candidate resonant structures RiR_iRi​.
Each has different:

lifetime,
coupling,
resistance to perturbation,
ability to recruit compatible structure,
access to energy and substrate,
compatibility or incompatibility with other structures.

Some disappear quickly.
Some persist.
Some spread.
Some coexist.
Thus an abstract selection process appears:
variation→differential persistence→different environmental impact\boxed{
\text{variation}
\rightarrow
\text{differential persistence}
\rightarrow
\text{different environmental impact}
}variation→differential persistence→different environmental impact​
without introducing a separate fundamental command saying "select the strongest".
The word strongest should itself be avoided unless the metric is defined. Stability, replication rate, spatial reach, coupling strength, and energetic efficiency are different quantities.
A better statement is:

Persistence and propagation can increase a structure’s contribution to its later environment; their importance depends on coupling, resources and the kind of influence being measured. This is not a universal ranking of structures.

That background is history made physical.

11. The lower level becomes the effective background of the next
This is the key recursive move, but it contains two different operations.
Physical change: realized lower-level structures and their interactions alter the environment. For example, their arrangement can change a field, boundary, chemical condition or transport pathway. This is an actual dynamical effect, whether or not anyone changes their description.
(Bn,{Rn}realized,interactions and resources)→physical evolutionBn′.(B_n,\{R_n\}_{\mathrm{realized}},\text{interactions and resources})
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{physical\ evolution}} B_n'.(Bn​,{Rn​}realized​,interactions and resources)physical evolution​Bn′​.
Change of description: at a larger or slower scale, some lower-level detail is unresolved. A reduction then describes selected collective variables and the remaining effective background:
Bn+1=Cn[Bn′,{Rn}realized].B_{n+1}=\mathcal C_n[B_n',\{R_n\}_{\mathrm{realized}}].Bn+1​=Cn​[Bn′​,{Rn​}realized​].
The map Cn\mathcal C_nCn​ does not itself physically make a new structure. A useful higher-level object must also exist and persist in the underlying system. This distinction prevents an ordinary mathematical coarse-graining from being mistaken for evidence of physical recursive construction.
The background may retain characteristic spectra, spatial correlations, memory, boundaries, mean fields and energy exchange. It need not be white noise. Mori’s reduction 06, E14 is a relevant mathematical example of unresolved dynamics appearing as memory and effective fluctuations; it is not a full RRG formation experiment.
This preserves the intended statement:

What is organized at one scale can become the material, constraints and unresolved activity from which organization emerges at the next.

The lower level remains physically active. Several levels can coexist, branch or fail to produce another level.

12. The same operation can now run again
Once Bn+1B_{n+1}Bn+1​ exists, new candidate geometries can appear within it:
Bn+1→{Gn+1(i)}.B_{n+1}
\rightarrow
\{G_{n+1}^{(i)}\}.Bn+1​→{Gn+1(i)​}.
Most are transient.
A stable closure produces:
Gn+1(∗)↔Mn+1(∗)G_{n+1}^{(*)}
\leftrightarrow
M_{n+1}^{(*)}Gn+1(∗)​↔Mn+1(∗)​
and therefore:
Rn+1=(Gn+1(∗),Mn+1(∗)).\boxed{
R_{n+1}
=(G_{n+1}^{(*)},M_{n+1}^{(*)}).
}Rn+1​=(Gn+1(∗)​,Mn+1(∗)​).​
Then:
Rn+1→Bn+2.R_{n+1}
\rightarrow
B_{n+2}.Rn+1​→Bn+2​.
The source operation repeats:
Bn→Rn→Bn+1.\boxed{
B_n
\rightarrow
R_n
\rightarrow
B_{n+1}.
}Bn​→Rn​→Bn+1​.​
This is the most compact form of the theory developed in this session.

13. Each level opens a new possibility space
Let:
Pn\boxed{\mathcal P_n}Pn​​
be the set of dynamically accessible organizations in background BnB_nBn​.
Because RnR_nRn​ changes the background:
Bn→Bn+1,B_n\rightarrow B_{n+1},Bn​→Bn+1​,
the accessible set can also change:
Pn→Pn+1.\boxed{
\mathcal P_n
\rightarrow
\mathcal P_{n+1}.
}Pn​→Pn+1​.​
This is more than creating additional copies of old objects.
A new persistent unit can make previously inaccessible combinations feasible under the changed conditions, including:

combinations,
relative positions,
bonds,
collective phases,
boundaries,
frequencies,
information-bearing states,
interaction networks,
catalytic pathways,
composite geometries.

Therefore:
stable organization→new effective degrees of freedom→new possible organization\boxed{
\text{stable organization}
\rightarrow
\text{new effective degrees of freedom}
\rightarrow
\text{new possible organization}
}stable organization→new effective degrees of freedom→new possible organization​
“New effective degrees of freedom” means new useful collective variables or accessible arrangements, not an automatic increase in the underlying microscopic state-space dimension. The accessible set may gain some organizations and lose others; a monotonic size comparison needs a defined measure and matched conditions.
Complexity does not have to be the objective.
It can be a consequence of repeatedly creating reusable stable units.
A more precise slogan is:
complexity becomes a new simple unit for the next scale.\boxed{
\text{complexity becomes a new simple unit for the next scale}.
}complexity becomes a new simple unit for the next scale.​

14. "The previous level already created what it can" — precise version
The intuitive session statement was:

each level creates what it can; then the stable result creates the space for something new.

The careful version is:
For background BnB_nBn​, define the stable set:
S(Bn)={R: R is dynamically accessible and persistent under Bn}.\boxed{
\mathcal S(B_n)
=
\{R:\ R\text{ is dynamically accessible and persistent under }B_n\}.
}S(Bn​)={R: R is dynamically accessible and persistent under Bn​}.​
The level need not literally explore every mathematical possibility.
Instead, the dynamics select some persistent subset of what is accessible.
As that persistent subset becomes part of the environment:
{Rn}→Bn+1,\{R_n\}
\rightarrow
B_{n+1},{Rn​}→Bn+1​,
the stable set can change:
S(Bn+1)≠S(Bn).\boxed{
\mathcal S(B_{n+1})
\neq\mathcal S(B_n).
}S(Bn+1​)=S(Bn​).​
Thus genuinely new organizations can become accessible only after earlier structures exist.
This is the proposed interpretation behind the phrase; the equation names an intended change rather than deriving it:

RRG proposes that the universe can recursively create conditions in which previously inaccessible organizations become persistent.


15. Effective laws: a new background can create a new effective world
The phrase "new laws" must be handled carefully.
RRG does not yet claim that each new level rewrites the deepest underlying law.
Instead, use the existing effective-action language:
Γn[R;Bn].\boxed{
\Gamma_n[R;B_n].
}Γn​[R;Bn​].​
The background affects:

which modes exist,
which modes propagate,
which interactions are screened or enhanced,
which structures are stable,
which collective variables matter,
which symmetries are realized,

37. How objections and failures should change the project
Every objection should identify what it addresses: a sentence in the conceptual framework, one toy equation, an empirical interpretation, or a stronger universal conjecture.
A failed toy implementation rejects that implementation or shows it needs revision. It is not automatically a disproof of the whole idea. Conversely, success of one engineered model is not a universal confirmation.
A result contradicting a precise universal statement is a substantive objection to that statement. Examples that stop, coexist, or reorganize without resonance are particularly useful for deciding which claims should be conditional. A fundamental-physics implementation must confront conservation laws and measured physical constraints; a cosmological implementation must address metric expansion rather than merely domain growth.
Lack of a distinctive prediction is a current evidential limitation, not a ban on publishing a clearly labelled hypothesis. Making definitions so broad that every possible result fits would weaken the framework’s scientific usefulness. The response is to record what a concrete version includes and excludes, not to demand a universal proof before discussion.
Counterarguments, unresolved findings and changes belong in the version history. They should not be silently deleted or turned into unrelated new definitions.

37. How objections and failures should change the project
Every objection should identify what it addresses: a sentence in the conceptual framework, one toy equation, an empirical interpretation, or a stronger universal conjecture.
A failed toy implementation rejects that implementation or shows it needs revision. It is not automatically a disproof of the whole idea. Conversely, success of one engineered model is not a universal confirmation.
A result contradicting a precise universal statement is a substantive objection to that statement. Examples that stop, coexist, or reorganize without resonance are particularly useful for deciding which claims should be conditional. A fundamental-physics implementation must confront conservation laws and measured physical constraints; a cosmological implementation must address metric expansion rather than merely domain growth.
Lack of a distinctive prediction is a current evidential limitation, not a ban on publishing a clearly labelled hypothesis. Making definitions so broad that every possible result fits would weaken the framework’s scientific usefulness. The response is to record what a concrete version includes and excludes, not to demand a universal proof before discussion.
Counterarguments, unresolved findings and changes belong in the version history. They should not be silently deleted or turned into unrelated new definitions.

Biological self-maintenance and reproduction are treated as advanced realizations of a similar abstract organizational logic, not as evidence that cells and fundamental particles use identical mechanisms.
Lock 12 — cosmic expansion remains an open derivation target
It is not yet evidence specific to RRG until the theory quantitatively derives metric/scale-factor dynamics.

39. Open conjectures generated by the session
The following are important but remain explicitly open.
C1 — Possibility-space growth
A genuinely new persistent effective unit tends to enlarge a meaningful measure of accessible organization:
μ(Pn+1)>μ(Pn).\mu(\mathcal P_{n+1})>\mu(\mathcal P_n).μ(Pn+1​)>μ(Pn​).
The correct measure μ\muμ is unknown.
C2 — Timescale hierarchy
Successive collective levels often have characteristic timescales longer than their internal components:
τn+1>τn\tau_{n+1}>\tau_nτn+1​>τn​
in a statistical rather than universal sense.
C3 — Recursive persistence generates apparent directionality
A history of stable background transformations may create an arrow of organizational development even if the underlying microscopic law is time-symmetric.
C4 — Effective-law hierarchy
Successive stable backgrounds may generate successively new effective theories:
Γ0→Γ1→Γ2→⋯\Gamma_0\rightarrow\Gamma_1\rightarrow\Gamma_2\rightarrow\cdotsΓ0​→Γ1​→Γ2​→⋯
while remaining descendants of one source-level mathematical family.
C5 — Spacetime connection
Physical spacetime geometry may itself be part of, or emerge from, the recursive resonant background structure.
C6 — Engineering inversion
If the forward map
(G,M)→Leff(G,M)\rightarrow L^{\rm eff}(G,M)→Leff
can be understood sufficiently well, it may be invertible enough to design desired effective dynamics:
Ltargeteff→(G,M)design.L_{\rm target}^{\rm eff}
\rightarrow
(G,M)_{\rm design}.Ltargeteff​→(G,M)design​.
This is the mathematical core of the "magic" engineering idea.

40. Publication and review priorities
The immediate sequence is: explain the source idea simply; give the full conceptual discussion; attach categorized examples and limits; publish the hypothesis for independent discussion. Mathematics is an optional companion.
For each later review, look for better evidence for a specific connection, corrections to existing sources, informative alternative explanations, and cases linking two stages in one physical system. Update the catalogue and claim map before enlarging the theory’s claims. Record why a change was made.
The author does not need to become a specialist or personally supply every proof. Contributors may offer cases, objections, derivations, code or experiments. A useful publication can distinguish these contributions without treating absence of a universal proof as project failure.
No automatic literature monitoring or background research is running. Reviews occur when requested or undertaken by project contributors.

41. Compact master formulation
The full session can be compressed into one recursive statement:

or:

\textbf{background}

The deepest current RRG sentence is:

Persistent resonance turns previous dynamics into the substrate for new resonance.

A second equivalent statement is:

What is organized structure at one level can become the effective background from which organization emerges at the next.

And the strongest research hypothesis is:

One recursive geometry–mode source process may generate multiple effective worlds, rather than nature requiring an independent fundamental construction rule for every level.


42. Verified evidence map
The active bibliography is 06 — Evidence catalogue, backed by sources.json (original source file). It separates result type from relevance and records what was checked.
Synchronization: E01. Mode-dependent particle motion: E02–E03. Noise-assisted model ordering and uniform-state patterns: E04–E05. Driven chemical reorganization: E06. This document does not claim that the complete Unity/RRG theory has been proved.

4. A background responds to an imposed constant intensity
For uniform variables, assume

If intensity actually depends on the evolving background, the equilibrium is implicit:
B∗=B0+ρI∗(B∗).B_*=B_0+\rho I_*(B_*).B∗​=B0​+ρI∗​(B∗​).
In a justified one-dimensional adiabatic reduction, its local linear growth rate is

Resetting B0B_0B0​ manually after every “level” builds a discrete update into the model; it does not establish autonomous recursion.
5. A damped candidate mode can become unstable
Suppose a previously specified candidate mode has a linear coefficient
λ(B)=rnext+α(B−B0),rnext<0.\lambda(B)=r_{\mathrm{next}}+\alpha(B-B_0),\qquad r_{\mathrm{next}}<0.λ(B)=rnext​+α(B−B0​),rnext​<0.
Under the constant-intensity assumption above, its asymptotic coefficient is positive when
αρI∗>−rnext.\alpha\rho I_*>-r_{\mathrm{next}}.αρI∗​>−rnext​.
This is algebraic substitution into an assumed coupling. The coefficient α\alphaα, sign of the feedback, candidate mode and background equation were not derived from the source principle.
The correct interpretation is: a linearly damped mode becomes linearly unstable. A negative growth rate never meant the mode was physically impossible or incapable of being excited by noise or forcing. A positive growth rate does not establish nonlinear saturation, stable geometry, coherent resonance or a new effective unit. A finite-domain pattern model also requires the wavenumber-detuning penalty from section 1.
This may be a useful local mechanism to investigate, but it is not itself a proof of Rn→Rn+1R_n\to R_{n+1}Rn​→Rn+1​.
6. Increasing length follows only from a specified scale response
For a differentiable preferred wavenumber q(B)>0q(B)>0q(B)>0, define ℓ(B)=2π/q(B)\ell(B)=2\pi/q(B)ℓ(B)=2π/q(B). Then
ℓ′(B)=−2πq′(B)q(B)2.\ell'(B)=-\frac{2\pi q'(B)}{q(B)^2}.ℓ′(B)=−q(B)22πq′(B)​.
If q′<0q'<0q′<0 throughout an interval and BBB increases across that interval, ℓ\ellℓ increases. If q′>0q'>0q′>0, the implication reverses. On a finite domain, the realized selected mode can change discretely and need not exactly follow this continuous preferred wavelength.
For the chosen example q(B)=q0e−σBq(B)=q_0e^{-\sigma B}q(B)=q0​e−σB, σ>0\sigma>0σ>0,
ℓ(B+ΔB)ℓ(B)=eσΔB.\frac{\ell(B+\Delta B)}{\ell(B)}=e^{\sigma\Delta B}.ℓ(B)ℓ(B+ΔB)​=eσΔB.
This identity does not derive the exponential choice. The earlier eight-level growth plot repeatedly supplied background increments; it was an illustration of those assumptions, not a simulated discovery of eight spontaneously arising physical levels.
A characteristic material wavelength is not the cosmological scale factor. A separate metric model would be required for that identification. Likewise, accelerated expansion and expansion are not synonymous. No cosmological conclusion follows from this wavelength calculation.
7. An error bound is not a proof that errors diverge
Assume, after specifying compatible maps, norms and time rescalings, that a nonnegative error sequence obeys
en+1≤ε+Ken,e0=0,K,ε≥0.e_{n+1}\le\varepsilon+Ke_n,\qquad e_0=0,\quad K,\varepsilon\ge0.en+1​≤ε+Ken​,e0​=0,K,ε≥0.
Repeated substitution gives
eN≤ε∑j=0N−1Kj.e_N\le\varepsilon\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}K^j.eN​≤εj=0∑N−1​Kj.
For K<1K<1K<1, this yields the sufficient uniform bound eN≤ε/(1−K)e_N\le\varepsilon/(1-K)eN​≤ε/(1−K). For K=1K=1K=1, it gives eN≤Nεe_N\le N\varepsiloneN​≤Nε. For K>1K>1K>1, the upper bound grows exponentially, but actual errors need not grow. The sequence en=0e_n=0en​=0 satisfies the inequality for every K≥0K\ge0K≥0 and ε≥0\varepsilon\ge0ε≥0.
Therefore a noncontractive bound neither disproves recursive behavior nor proves actual instability. Conversely, the existence of a contracting abstract inequality does not show that a physical coarse-graining satisfies it.
In the previous note, bounds for the higher-level flow alone were treated as sufficient to get this recurrence. A real multi-level comparison also needs control of reduction maps, state domains, normalization, parameter changes and aligned times. The recurrence is an explicit assumption here, not a derived general fact about RRG.
8. What is inserted, and what is obtained

These simple results may help someone develop a more complete model. They do not need to be promoted into a universal proof to be useful. Some further work may be possible; this audit has not attempted it.
9. Verification actually performed in this release
The standard-library script checks/verify_small_results.py (original source file) checks fixed-point residuals and derivatives, the stationary-density current identity, finite-domain detuning, the relaxation equation, the implicit-background stability example, scale monotonicity and the error-bound counterexample. Results are written to checks/verification_results.json (original source file).
These are deterministic algebra/numerical spot checks, not independent peer review, full stochastic simulations or formal machine-checked theorems. The earlier 32-cell research simulation and its claimed convergence checks are preserved but were not rerun in this audit.
10. A useful contribution can be smaller than a proof
A reader may identify a mistaken assumption, derive one actual geometry-dependent response, connect two steps in a measured system, or provide a counterexample. All are worthwhile. None requires accepting the entire framework first. The immediate public package remains the source-direction explanation plus 06 — Evidence catalogue.
Historical archive availability
References to archive/ in this source describe historical companion material. Those files are excluded from this website and its publication ZIP. The owner-supplied original bundle has been captured privately: its ten current scientific documents match the selected edition, and its inner package checks pass. The outer checksum manifest contains a self-hash discrepancy; off-machine backup is not verified. This is provenance comparison, not a new scientific approval. Repository predecessor readings remain explicitly historical in the document library.

RRG v0.2.1 · checked 2 October 2026 · living publication companion
RRG proposes that persistent geometry–mode organization can change the background in which further organization becomes possible. This catalogue explains the real observations and limited mathematical results that make parts of that idea worth considering. It does not require a universal proof before the hypothesis is shared.
The key reading rule: an established component is evidence that a mechanism can occur under the reported conditions. Its interpretation as one stage of RRG is a separate claim. Different examples do not automatically combine into one demonstrated recursive chain.
Two labels, not one evidence ladder
What kind of result? Experiment; simulation; theoretical/mathematical derivation. A study can contain more than one. A review is an orientation source rather than an extra experiment. Internal RRG calculations are separately labelled and not counted as independent support.
How does it relate? A component demonstrates a local operation; a partial bridge connects operations in one system; an analogy shares organizational logic without demonstrating the same microscopic process; a constraint/comparator identifies limits or an alternative mechanism. None of these labels is a confidence score for all of RRG.
Claim map



Claim
Limited operation being discussed




C0
Fluctuations or a uniform starting regime can participate in pattern formation or interaction.


C1
Geometry and mode structure constrain or affect one another.


C2
Coupled oscillators can develop collective phase/frequency relationships.


C3
A driven field or vibration can reorganize material.


C4
An organization, boundary or interaction changes what its surroundings can do.


C5
A nonliving pattern or chemical organization can propagate or multiply.


C6
Lower-level dynamics admit useful collective variables and an effective background description.


C7
Controlled conditions can implement selected effective dynamics.



These are not eight already-proved stages in the history of the universe. C0, for example, distinguishes noise-induced ordering from deterministic instability. C6 distinguishes a physical new environment from our mathematical description of it.
Start with these connections
For the source-direction intuition, begin with E19 (random-field-mediated interaction) and E04 (noise-assisted pattern formation in a model). For reciprocal organization, use E07/E08/E18. For multiplication without life, use E10/E11/E20. For the next-level background, read E14/E21 together with their limits. E17 and E22 prevent the catalogue from turning all organization into evidence for stronger resonance.

E01 — Experimental Study of the Triplet Synchronization of Coupled Nonidentical Mechanical Metronomes
experiment · component / constraint · claims C2.
Reported result: Coupled nonidentical metronomes exhibit a collective triplet synchronization relation even where individual pairs are asynchronous.
Already supplied: Metronomes, their energy supply, and mechanical coupling already exist.
Limit of the RRG connection: Collective coordination need not mean every oscillator has one identical frequency or phase. This does not demonstrate the creation of the oscillators.
Source: Jia, Song, Liu, Kurths & Xiao (2015), Scientific Reports 5, 17008. DOI: 10.1038/srep17008.
Verification coverage: Publisher HTML, including experimental description. Checked 2026-10-02.
E02 — Controlling the motion of multiple objects on a Chladni plate
experiment · component · claims C1, C3.
Reported result: Plate vibrations can transport particles; the study uses controlled sequences of excitation to manipulate multiple objects.
Already supplied: A manufactured plate, particles, actuator, camera and control algorithm are provided.
Limit of the RRG connection: Distinguish ordinary nodal accumulation from the paper’s actively controlled manipulation. Neither establishes autonomous particle-to-field feedback or reproduction.
Source: Zhou, Sariola, Latifi & Liimatainen (2016), Nature Communications 7, 12764. DOI: 10.1038/ncomms12764.
Verification coverage: Publisher HTML and author-institution abstract. Supplementary videos linked on the paper page were not watched. Checked 2026-10-02.
E03 — Independent trapping and manipulation of microparticles using dexterous acoustic tweezers
experiment · component · claims C3.
Reported result: A phased ultrasonic array independently traps and manipulates microparticles; reported examples include 45 and 90 micrometre spheres.
Already supplied: An engineered transducer array, liquid medium and pre-existing particles are required.
Limit of the RRG connection: This particular experiment supports microscale manipulation, not a claim of nanoscale performance or a universal size–frequency law.
Source: Courtney et al. (2014), Applied Physics Letters 104, 154103. DOI: 10.1063/1.4870489.
Verification coverage: Author-institution records and original-paper abstract; not a full methods or data audit. Checked 2026-10-02.
E04 — Noise-induced spatial periodicity in excitable chemical media
simulation · component · claims C0.
Reported result: Numerical excitable-chemical-media dynamics show an intermediate noise regime with enhanced spatial periodicity.
Already supplied: An Oregonator-type reaction model, diffusion, parameter choices and noisy forcing are specified.
Limit of the RRG connection: This is a numerical result, not a laboratory observation of the primordial background. Noise acts through existing nonlinear dynamics.
Source: Matjaž Perc (2005), Chemical Physics Letters 410, 49–53. DOI: 10.1016/j.cplett.2005.05.042.
Verification coverage: Primary publisher record and abstract; equations and simulation data not independently reproduced. Checked 2026-10-02.
E05 — Transition from a uniform state to hexagonal and striped Turing patterns
experiment · component / comparator · claims C0.
Reported result: A chemically supplied reaction–diffusion experiment produces stationary patterned states from a uniform regime.
Already supplied: Specific reactions, diffusion, gel geometry and reagent supply are provided.
Limit of the RRG connection: A stationary spatial mode is not automatically a temporal oscillation or a self-maintaining resonator. Uniform-state instability is not identical to noise-induced ordering.
Source: Ouyang & Swinney (1991), Nature 352, 610–612. DOI: 10.1038/352610a0.
Verification coverage: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record. Checked 2026-10-02.
E06 — Resonant pattern formation in a chemical system
experiment · partial bridge · claims C2, C3.
Reported result: Periodic illumination of a photosensitive chemical oscillator locks responses to the forcing and changes the spatial pattern.
Already supplied: The reaction medium and periodic optical drive are supplied externally.
Limit of the RRG connection: The experiment links temporal forcing and spatial organization, not the spontaneous origin of the drive or new fundamental laws.
Source: Petrov, Ouyang & Swinney (1997), Nature 388, 655–657. DOI: 10.1038/41732.
Verification coverage: Publisher abstract and record. Checked 2026-10-02.
E07 — Dicke quantum phase transition with a superfluid gas in an optical cavity
experiment · partial bridge · claims C1, C3, C4.
Reported result: A pumped atom–cavity system undergoes a collective transition with mutually coupled matter organization and optical-field dynamics.
Already supplied: Atoms, cavity boundaries and laser pumping are given.
Limit of the RRG connection: This is a close geometry–field feedback example, but not unstructured matter producing its own complete apparatus or successive autonomous levels.
Source: Baumann, Guerlin, Brennecke & Esslinger (2010), Nature 464, 1301–1306. DOI: 10.1038/nature09009.
Verification coverage: Publisher abstract and article record. Checked 2026-10-02.
E08 — Tunable colloidal swarmalators with hydrodynamic coupling
experiment · partial bridge · claims C1, C2, C3.
Reported result: Colloidal oscillator phases and spatial organization co-evolve in collective states.
Already supplied: Feedback-controlled active particles and hydrodynamic interactions are part of the experimental mechanism.
Limit of the RRG connection: The control architecture is essential context; it cannot be omitted when describing how spontaneous the organization is.
Source: Heuthe, Iyer, Gompper & Bechinger (2025), Nature Communications 16, 10984. DOI: 10.1038/s41467-025-66830-5.
Verification coverage: Publisher HTML, including setup/control description. Checked 2026-10-02. Published 8 December 2025. The experiment is not a demonstration of an unprogrammed universal source law.
E09 — Self-Organized Resonance during Search of a Diverse Chemical Space
simulation · partial bridge · claims C1, C4.
Reported result: A driven reacting-particle model develops structures matched to periodic forcing; in the studied regime their energy absorption helps stabilization.
Already supplied: Toy reaction rules, Brownian dynamics and a periodic drive are specified.
Limit of the RRG connection: This is not laboratory evidence and does not show that maximum absorption is a universal selection rule. Compare E17.
Source: Kachman, Owen & England (2017), Physical Review Letters 119, 038001. DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.038001.
Verification coverage: Original-paper abstract on APS and author-institution record. Checked 2026-10-02.
E10 — Experimental observation of self-replicating spots in a reaction–diffusion system
experiment · partial bridge · claims C5.
Reported result: Chemical spots grow and split repeatedly in a laboratory reaction–diffusion system.
Already supplied: Reactive chemicals and nonequilibrium experimental conditions are supplied.
Limit of the RRG connection: Pattern duplication is not automatically reproduction with heredity, or a new organizational level. Do not infer a resonant microscopic mechanism merely from the shared shape of the process.
Source: Lee, McCormick, Pearson & Swinney (1994), Nature 369, 215–218. DOI: 10.1038/369215a0.
Verification coverage: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record. Checked 2026-10-02.
E11 — Self-Replicating Holes in a Vertically Vibrated Dense Suspension
experiment · partial bridge · claims C3, C5.
Reported result: Holes in a vertically driven starch suspension deform and split under suitable forcing.
Already supplied: The suspension, container and sustained vertical vibration already exist.
Limit of the RRG connection: A hole is a spatial pattern in supplied material, not a newly manufactured independent resonator or organism. Shape instability is part of replication here.
Source: Ebata & Sano (2011), Physical Review Letters 107, 088301. DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.088301.
Verification coverage: Original-paper abstract on APS. Checked 2026-10-02.
E12 — Dynamic self-assembly of magnetized, millimetre-sized objects rotating at a liquid–air interface
experiment · partial bridge · claims C3, C4.
Reported result: Magnetically driven objects organize through their motion and fluid-mediated interactions.
Already supplied: Fabricated magnetic objects, liquid interface and rotating external field are provided.
Limit of the RRG connection: The result connects maintained activity and spatial arrangement. It does not imply all stable structures need continuous external driving.
Source: Grzybowski, Stone & Whitesides (2000), Nature 405, 1033–1036. DOI: 10.1038/35016528.
Verification coverage: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record. Checked 2026-10-02.
E13 — Spontaneous network formation among cooperative RNA replicators
experiment · structural analogue / partial bridge · claims C5, C4.
Reported result: RNA fragments assemble into catalytic networks; tested cooperative networks have growth advantages over competing autocatalytic cycles.
Already supplied: Selected RNA sequences, fragments and controlled chemical conditions are supplied.
Limit of the RRG connection: This supports chemical organizational feedback and cooperation, not an identical acoustic or fundamental-particle mechanism. A formal catalytic graph alone does not establish sustained kinetics.
Source: Vaidya, Manapat, Chen, Xulvi-Brunet, Hayden & Lehman (2012), Nature 491, 72–77. DOI: 10.1038/nature11549.
Verification coverage: Publisher abstract and change history; full subscription methods not inspected. Checked 2026-10-02. Publisher reports a minor Figure 1 typo corrected on 31 October 2012. No claim here depends on the corrected figure.
E14 — Transport, Collective Motion, and Brownian Motion
theory / mathematical derivation · partial bridge · claims C6.
Reported result: Projection of many-body dynamics leads to a reduced description involving collective variables, memory and effective fluctuating forces.
Already supplied: Microscopic dynamics and a projection/choice of resolved variables are supplied.
Limit of the RRG connection: Unresolved dynamics need not be white noise. Describing a system at lower resolution does not physically create a new medium or hierarchy.
Source: Hazime Mori (1965), Progress of Theoretical Physics 33, 423–455. DOI: 10.1143/PTP.33.423.
Verification coverage: Original publisher abstract and record; historical derivation not independently re-proved. Checked 2026-10-02.
E15 — Realization of the Hofstadter Hamiltonian with Ultracold Atoms in Optical Lattices
experiment · partial bridge · claims C7.
Reported result: Laser-assisted tunnelling implements an effective lattice Hamiltonian with magnetic-field-like phases.
Already supplied: Cold atoms, an optical lattice and precisely controlled driving are provided.
Limit of the RRG connection: This demonstrates selected effective dynamics, not arbitrary alteration of fundamental laws or a frequency-only recipe.
Source: Aidelsburger, Atala, Lohse, Barreiro, Paredes & Bloch (2013), Physical Review Letters 111, 185301. DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.185301.
Verification coverage: Original-paper abstract on APS. Checked 2026-10-02.
E16 — A colloidal viewpoint on the sausage catastrophe and the finite sphere packing problem
experiment and simulation · component / comparator · claims C4.
Reported result: Confinement of colloidal spheres in vesicles influences which packing geometries occur, including competing arrangements.
Already supplied: Pre-existing particles, confining membranes and their material properties are provided.
Limit of the RRG connection: This is evidence that geometry affects accessible organization, not evidence that every such effect requires resonance.
Source: Marín-Aguilar et al. (2023), Nature Communications 14, 7896. DOI: 10.1038/s41467-023-43722-0.
Verification coverage: Publisher HTML; not an independent reproduction of simulations. Checked 2026-10-02.
E17 — Drive-specific selection in multistable mechanical networks
simulation; published report also includes experimental evidence · constraint · claims C4.
Reported result: In studied driven mechanical networks, selected configurations absorb relatively little work from the drive.
Already supplied: Multistable spring networks, their interaction landscape and an external drive are supplied.
Limit of the RRG connection: This constrains “strongest resonance always dominates”; it does not refute a conditional geometry–mode hypothesis. The experimental portion was not separately method-audited here.
Source: Kedia, Pan, Slotine & England (2023), Journal of Chemical Physics 159, 214106. DOI: 10.1063/5.0171993.
Verification coverage: Author preprint arXiv:1908.09332 plus journal metadata and original abstract indexed by PubMed. Checked 2026-10-02. The 2019 preprint title is Drive-specific adaptation in disordered mechanical networks of bistable springs. It is not an additional independent study.
E18 — Optical binding
experiment · partial bridge · claims C3, C4.
Reported result: Illuminated microspheres display light-mediated interactions and bound configurations.
Already supplied: An external optical field, microspheres and surrounding medium already exist.
Limit of the RRG connection: Field scattering and particle arrangement interact, but a bound pair is not yet a recursively reproducing hierarchy.
Source: Burns, Fournier & Golovchenko (1989), Physical Review Letters 63, 1233–1236. DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.63.1233.
Verification coverage: Original-paper abstract and record on APS. Checked 2026-10-02.
E19 — Controlling dispersion forces between small particles with artificially created random light fields
experiment and theory · partial bridge · claims C0, C4.
Reported result: Artificially generated random light produces measured attractive interactions between dielectric microspheres.
Already supplied: Pre-existing spheres and a laser-generated, quasi-monochromatic random optical field are provided.
Limit of the RRG connection: Random does not mean broadband white noise. The experiment supports fluctuation-mediated interaction, not spontaneous creation of the spheres; broader interaction designs include theoretical proposals.
Source: Brügger, Froufe-Pérez, Scheffold & Sáenz (2015), Nature Communications 6, 7460. DOI: 10.1038/ncomms8460.
Verification coverage: Publisher HTML, including experimental versus theoretical scope. Checked 2026-10-02.
E20 — Self-replicating segregation patterns in horizontally vibrated binary mixture of granules
experiment · partial bridge · claims C3, C4, C5.
Reported result: A shaken granular mixture develops bands that reproduce; segregation and flow/fluidity feedback participate in the dynamics.
Already supplied: Two grain populations, a container and continued horizontal shaking are supplied.

RRG v0.2.1 · checked 2 October 2026 · living publication companion
RRG proposes that persistent geometry–mode organization can change the background in which further organization becomes possible. This catalogue explains the real observations and limited mathematical results that make parts of that idea worth considering. It does not require a universal proof before the hypothesis is shared.
The key reading rule: an established component is evidence that a mechanism can occur under the reported conditions. Its interpretation as one stage of RRG is a separate claim. Different examples do not automatically combine into one demonstrated recursive chain.
Two labels, not one evidence ladder
What kind of result? Experiment; simulation; theoretical/mathematical derivation. A study can contain more than one. A review is an orientation source rather than an extra experiment. Internal RRG calculations are separately labelled and not counted as independent support.
How does it relate? A component demonstrates a local operation; a partial bridge connects operations in one system; an analogy shares organizational logic without demonstrating the same microscopic process; a constraint/comparator identifies limits or an alternative mechanism. None of these labels is a confidence score for all of RRG.
Claim map



Claim
Limited operation being discussed




C0
Fluctuations or a uniform starting regime can participate in pattern formation or interaction.


C1
Geometry and mode structure constrain or affect one another.


C2
Coupled oscillators can develop collective phase/frequency relationships.


C3
A driven field or vibration can reorganize material.


C4
An organization, boundary or interaction changes what its surroundings can do.


C5
A nonliving pattern or chemical organization can propagate or multiply.


C6
Lower-level dynamics admit useful collective variables and an effective background description.


C7
Controlled conditions can implement selected effective dynamics.



These are not eight already-proved stages in the history of the universe. C0, for example, distinguishes noise-induced ordering from deterministic instability. C6 distinguishes a physical new environment from our mathematical description of it.
Start with these connections
For the source-direction intuition, begin with E19 (random-field-mediated interaction) and E04 (noise-assisted pattern formation in a model). For reciprocal organization, use E07/E08/E18. For multiplication without life, use E10/E11/E20. For the next-level background, read E14/E21 together with their limits. E17 and E22 prevent the catalogue from turning all organization into evidence for stronger resonance.

RRG v0.2.1 · 2 October 2026
This map prevents two kinds of drift: losing the author’s bigger idea when tightening scientific language, and turning a proposed connection into a verified fact. “Preserved” means the idea remains in the publication, not that it has been established.

H01
Start with fluctuating activity, not pre-built resonators
04 §§2–4
Source hypothesis. A fluctuating background still needs defined dynamics in an implementation.


H02
Transient arrangements appear; some become persistent
04 §§2–5, 18
Component precedents E04/E05. These do not establish the primordial origin of matter.


H03
Geometry and frequency/mode form a feedback loop
04 §§1, 5, 19
Core proposal; E07/E08 are partial physical bridges. Preserve the full mode definition.


H04
Oscillators influence one another through a shared medium
04 §6; E01
Experimental component. Collective synchronization need not mean identical phases/frequencies.


H05
Vibration can rearrange suitable material
04 §7; E02/E03/E20
Experimental component under stated coupling and forcing. Not every rearrangement is resonant.


H06
A formed structure reshapes the background around it
04 §§4, 11, 24
Key causal connection; partial bridges E07/E18/E19, with supplied apparatus explicit.


H07
Longer persistence gives more opportunity to influence
04 §8
Conditional interpretation, not inevitable growth or indefinitely accumulated energy.


H08
Repeated compatible arrangements can appear without a copying command
04 §§9–10
Proposed mechanism. Recurrence, synchronization, recruitment and independent reproduction differ.


H09
Domains compete, dominate or coexist
04 §§9–10
Conditional outcomes, not a single “strongest frequency always wins” law. E17 constrains it.


H10
Lower-level organization becomes noise-like substrate to the next level
04 §11; E14
Core conjectural use of effective background. Noise can be correlated and retain memory.


H11
The same abstract operation repeats in different effective worlds
04 §§12, 21, 25, 41
Central RRG hypothesis, not established by combining unrelated examples.


H12
Persistent combinations become new effective units
04 §§12–13, 22
Proposed hierarchy. A larger synchronized patch alone is not proof of a new unit.


H13

Publication companion v0.2.1 · audited 2 October 2026 · promoted to repository CURRENT 5 October 2026

Repository authority note. The owner has explicitly replaced the prior active publication/research companion with this audited v0.2.1 set. The project-wide minimal 00_LOCKED_CORE.md, current repository 01–03 foundation documents, and 05_CHANGE_CONTROL.md are carried forward unchanged; see SOURCE_AUTHORITY.md and CURRENT_MANIFEST.md.

RRG asks whether the same organizing process can repeat across scales: fluctuations produce temporary arrangements; some arrangements support activity that helps them persist; those persistent structures change their surroundings; the resulting environment offers conditions for further organization.
What is organized at one level can become the material, constraints and unresolved activity of the next. In the project’s notation:
Bn→Rn→Bn+1,Rn=(Gn,Mn),Gn↔Mn.B_n\rightarrow R_n\rightarrow B_{n+1},\qquad
R_n=(G_n,M_n),\qquad G_n\leftrightarrow M_n.Bn​→Rn​→Bn+1​,Rn​=(Gn​,Mn​),Gn​↔Mn​.
Here geometry means spatial and relational organization. Mode includes frequency, phase, amplitude, spatial pattern, coupling and timescale—not just a number in hertz. Background includes inherited structures and dynamics; it need not be literal white noise.
The project’s current purpose is to explain and share this proposed connection, collect well-described cases, and invite independent development. A universal proof is not required before publication. Small derivations, observations and objections can improve the framework without proving or refuting all of it at once.
Reading paths
First read the idea: 04 — Full conceptual companion. It preserves the whole session: source background, feedback, scale, persistence, propagation, coexistence, life, new effective rules, expansion and possible engineering implications.
Then inspect the examples: 06 — Evidence catalogue. There are 22 primary case cards, with separate labels for result type and relevance. Every card identifies the reported result, what was supplied, what it does not demonstrate, its DOI and verification coverage.
Check the boundaries without losing the ambition: 08 — Claims and session coverage. This distinguishes the author’s broad hypotheses from local evidence and avoids silently dropping life, cosmic expansion, AI or “magic” from the discussion.
Optional mathematics: 05 — Mathematical illustrations. These are small calculations under explicit assumptions, not proof that a single equation generates the universe. There is no requirement that the author adopt this model.
See what was repaired: 07 — Audit report and CHANGELOG.
A clear public evidence format
For each example, state what was observed, how RRG interprets it, what was already provided, and what remains open. Show result type separately: experiment, simulation or mathematical/theoretical derivation. Do not present an analogy as a measured mechanism, a review as an independent experiment, or a computation as an observation in nature.
Many standard theories already explain the reported effects. Showing compatibility with RRG is different from distinguishing RRG from those theories. A collection of separately supported connections is not automatically a demonstrated causal chain.
A useful entry point into the evidence is E19 for interactions induced by a random field, E07 for coupled matter–field organization, E20 for vibrationally maintained pattern multiplication, and E14 for unresolved dynamics in a collective description. Their limitations matter as much as the resemblance to the idea.
What is maintained, and what remains conjectural
The central source-direction idea is unchanged. So is the ambition that new stable organizations could help explain successive effective “worlds.” The publication does not silently replace that ambition with a claim merely about sand on a plate.
The extensions to all physical scales, the origin of fundamental interactions, cosmic expansion and deliberately designed domains are retained as open conjectures. Engineering selected effective dynamics is a narrower claim than rewriting fundamental laws. Life and AI are possible applications or analogies, not confirmations of a shared microscopic mechanism.
One further distinction is essential: structures physically changing their environment is different from our coarse-graining a system’s description. RRG proposes a relationship between the two, but a mathematical reduction by itself does not demonstrate that a new level physically formed.
History and file authority
The files in foundations/ are byte-preserved snapshots of 01–03. They preserve the terminology and prior development; they have not received a complete fresh source audit. Some contain older proof-first priorities, stronger mathematical assertions and a known formatting issue. Foundation errata records the compatibility corrections. They are not the current public evidence catalogue.
The former 04–06 text companions, old README and earlier numerical bundles remain preserved in the owner’s audited GPT Library release; the predecessor GitHub current set is separately preserved under research/history/repository-current-2026-10-01/. They are not duplicated inside the active RRG_CURRENT tree and do not define current publication guidance. The current README and audited 04–08 state this release’s publication scope. Where an earlier mathematical implementation is more restrictive than the conceptual proposal, treat it as an optional stronger branch rather than silently redefining the theory.
This audited package originated as a conversation/Library artifact and was explicitly promoted by the owner to replace the prior active repository companion on 5 October 2026. The predecessor repository source set is preserved under research/history/repository-current-2026-10-01/. This source promotion does not by itself qualify the website, grant a licence, or authorize a Pages deployment.
What was checked
The audit checked the current companions for conceptual consistency, verified targeted primary-source metadata and reported findings, corrected selected mathematics and ran nine groups of deterministic spot checks. See check results (original source file), source register (original source file) and package validation (original source file).
This is not independent peer review, a systematic review of all literature, formal verification, or an independent replication of the experiments. Some case cards are abstract-level checks. The earlier 32-cell simulation was not rerun. These limitations are recorded per source instead of hidden behind a numerical quality score.
Contributions and release practice
Useful contributions include simpler explanations, missing cases, counterexamples, corrected citations and optional derivations. Each change should identify which claim it affects. The author need not perform every proof personally; neither should unavailable proof be replaced by a statement of certainty.
Reviews occur when undertaken by the project; no automatic monitoring is running. Keep source dates, revisions and old interpretations so later readers can reconstruct changes. Use original source pages for videos and figures, and check reuse rights before embedding them. A citation is not a licence.
Before external publication, choose author attribution and a licence for the project’s own text/code. This package does not invent a real author name, assign third-party rights, select a software licence or guarantee a venue’s acceptance.

rows.rationale: The argument follows causal conditions from pH feedback to the missing connected-stage question, distinguishing supplied populations, physical background changes and descriptive units.

displays.priorCanonicalBodyText:
A population changes the next population's chances
Begin with bacteria in a liquid culture. Their growth can change its acidity. That change can help another population grow, inhibit it or harm the population that caused the change. Ratzke and Gore report these different outcomes in a controlled pH-feedback study.
The useful question is causal: what existed, what did it change, and what became possible afterward? The culture and organisms were supplied. The result is environmental feedback between existing populations, not a new species or an origin-of-life experiment.
Conditions are part of the mechanism
An inventory of ingredients leaves out the conditions under which they interact. A structure can contribute a boundary, maintain a gradient or change its chemical surroundings. The later system then encounters a different setting.
The source's star example develops this in another physical setting. A gravitationally organized star establishes temperature, pressure and reaction conditions; stellar evolution and dispersal of many heavier elements change the material available for later chemistry. The star reading keeps the mechanism and its limits visible.
These are different physical processes. Juxtaposing them does not demonstrate that they obey an identical microscopic equation. What they make intelligible is the question RRG wants to investigate: can the formation of a unit and its effect on later conditions be studied together?
Changing a background is different from naming a unit
A molecule can be treated as an intact participant in a later description. That reduces the details we track. Bacterial pH changes alter the environment itself, whether or not we change our description. One operation is descriptive; the other is physical.
The current recursive-background companion proposes a connection between them: a background supports organization; that organization changes the conditions inherited by what follows. It also asks where the first units arise, beginning with transient arrangements in an active background rather than a completed inventory of building blocks.
What would connect the stages?
The recursive physical construction question calls for causally connected stages in one system. To discuss such a case, identify the initial conditions, the formed organization, its environmental effect and the subsequent organization. Say which stages were observed and which were supplied or inferred.
A population growing after a pH change provides one bounded connection. It does not supply the whole source-to-repeated-level chain. Similarity between different examples can motivate a model; it cannot replace that missing causal connection.
A change can close possibilities too
The harmful and inhibitory culture outcomes matter. RRG's proposal is conditional: suitable coupling, resources and dynamics matter, and a process can stop, coexist, branch or destroy an organization. It is not a law that every change makes something larger or more complex.
The next useful question is therefore specific: which organization changes which conditions, for which subsequent process? Follow life and environmental change or inspect the source connections to trace a case with its actual support and limits.

displays.priorCanonicalBodyText:
Start with an intact molecule
A molecule contains atoms, electron states and collective motion. Yet another chemical description can treat it as one participant. We have not erased its parts; we have chosen the properties relevant to a particular interaction. The molecule example traces this back to the supplied world explanation.
Now change the question. If the molecule dissociates, continuing to count one intact participant hides a material change. A useful unit is therefore not simply whatever we can draw a boundary around. Its usefulness depends on the circumstances and the response we need to describe.
What can remain unresolved?
RRG asks which collective organization persists while its parts remain active. A later description may track an intact whole's motion, relationships or response without tracking every lower-level detail. If those hidden details affect the answer, the description needs to retain more of them.
This does not mean that all useful reductions are simple averages. The current background companion explains that correlations, mode patterns, coupling and memory may matter. Reducing everything to one number can discard the very relation that made a whole useful.
Organization and activity belong together
The registered RRG object is UT-D03. Its geometry includes relationships, boundaries and constraints. Its mode structure includes phases, coupling, responses and characteristic times, beyond one frequency.
The stability definition concerns self-consistent geometry–mode organization over an interval. It is not permanence, and it does not prescribe one lifetime threshold for molecules, cells and every other system.
The scale definition asks when a collective organization functions as an effective unit in further interactions. Parts can differ and remain internally active. The recursion definition permits further combination without requiring an identical microscopic mechanism or compulsory copying at every step.
A mathematical question with a stated scope
The candidate mathematics compares two routes: evolve the detailed system and then reduce it, or reduce it and predict the collective evolution. A useful comparison needs stated variables, maps, conditions and an error measure.
That is a model-specific research test. It does not establish that a new physical level formed, or require every scale to obey the same equation family. The stronger same-family question remains optional. No such calculation is executed in this article.
The whole has another possible role
A cell may be one participant in a larger organization while continuing its internal exchanges. Its activity may also change its surroundings. Treating the cell as a unit and measuring that environmental change answer different questions.
How existing structures make new organization possible follows the second role. Read the two together without assuming that success at one operation proves the complete recursive proposal.
The question to take into a concrete model is: for this interaction and interval, which collective properties suffice, and what would require us to describe the parts again? Explore recursion and scale for the shorter definition-led path.

Optical binding: illuminated microspheres show light-mediated interactions and bound arrangements. The light, particles and medium are already supplied. UT-E118
Controlled random light: an artificially generated random optical field produces measured attractive interactions between small spheres. Random does not mean broadband white noise, and the experiment does not create the spheres. UT-E119

displays.priorCanonicalBodyText:
In ordinary words
An organized whole can participate in another organization. Its internal activity continues even when the next description treats it as one useful unit. RRG calls this structural recursion.
A concrete example
The molecule example begins with atoms and their connections. A molecule can enter a larger chemical arrangement. A cell can participate in a tissue while exchanges and reactions continue inside it. These systems have different mechanisms; the shared description does not require identical equations at every scale.
Scale means a level at which a collective organization can function as an effective unit in further interactions. It involves characteristic times, dominant interactions and useful descriptions, as well as size. It is not a claim that all levels are equally spaced or every larger process is slower.
The source definitions
A collective organization can function as an effective unit in further interactions. Mechanisms may differ across scales.
UT-D05
Compatible lower-level systems may form a higher-level organization while retaining internal activity. Their components may differ.
UT-D06
Organized units may take part in further organization. This structural claim does not require an identical microscopic equation.
UT-D08
The proposed cycle is compatible parts → collective organization → a useful unit → further combinations. Its environment can also change which combinations are accessible. The cycle illustration represents a research proposal, not a measurement or guaranteed history.
A unit and a changed background are different roles
Treating a molecule as one participant changes our description. A living population changing a culture's acidity changes the physical conditions. Neither operation automatically establishes the other.
The current background proposal asks how these roles can connect. It also asks where the first units come from: transient arrangements arise in an active background; some may persist through feedback. This is a source hypothesis, not an observed universal history or a fixed upward ladder.
Copying is one possible mechanism
Replication is one possible way to form or propagate organization; it is not required at every level.
UT-D09
Replication, aggregation and self-assembly can participate in formation or propagation. Duplication is optional in the locked core. The stronger questions of a predictive cross-domain criterion and spontaneous promotion remain open.

displays.priorCanonicalBodyText:
In ordinary words
An organization can persist while activity continues inside it. In the supplied core, stability means that geometry and mode structure form a self-consistent closed organization during the interval in question. Persistence may be short or long.
Compare the questions
A molecule can be considered over a particular lifetime; a living cell needs ongoing exchanges. To test a specified model, we may measure how long a state lasts, how it responds to a perturbation or whether nearby states approach it.
Bounded persistence asks whether the chosen organization remains within stated limits over an interval. Recovery asks whether it returns after a disturbance. Attraction asks whether nearby states tend toward it. These describe different tests; observing one is not automatically a result about the others.
The framework allows different mathematical tests for different systems. They do not replace its locked meaning. A self-consistency definition is not an independently established universal stability theorem.

G↔M.\boxed{G\leftrightarrow M}.G↔M​.

Here GGG denotes organization and MMM the full temporal mode structure. Their reciprocal relation is the RRG definition being used. A particular application still needs its conditions, equations and evidence; the definition alone does not give a numerical threshold.

displays.priorCanonicalBodyText:
Four questions to carry into the examples
Geometry and mode structure
Core definitions. What is organized, and how does it move, change or respond? Geometry includes relationships and constraints; mode structure includes more than one frequency.
A string's fixed ends restrict its supported motions, while tension and material also matter. Explore geometry and modes.
Stability
Core definition. What lets an organization persist while its parts remain active? Persistence can involve maintaining, restoring or recreating the organized state. It is not a promise of permanence or a universal measurement of lifetime.
A cell exchanges material while remaining recognizable. Explore stability.
Scale and recursion
Core definitions; open generalization. When can a whole become a useful part of another description? A scale is an effective regime, not just a size. Recursion does not require identical parts or compulsory replication.
A molecule can act as one unit in further interactions while retaining internal structure. Explore recursion and scale.
Background and effective interactions
Current source-direction extension. How can existing organization change the conditions or interactions available to later structures?
Living systems can change their chemical surroundings. Light-mediated particle interactions show narrower local mechanisms with externally supplied fields. Explore effective interactions and the recursive background companion.
The minimal core and the current extension
The project-wide minimal locked core defines R=(G,M)R=(G,M)R=(G,M) and G↔MG\leftrightarrow MG↔M: organization and mode structure considered together.
The current companion centres the source-direction relation Bn→Rn→Bn+1B_n\rightarrow R_n\rightarrow B_{n+1}Bn​→Rn​→Bn+1​: a background supports organization, and that organization may change the background available for what follows. This is a central commitment of the current branch; it does not silently amend the older project-wide lock boundary. “Locked” means explicit change control, not empirical proof.
Whether one law works across repeated levels, or one mathematical equation family describes them all, remains a stronger open question. Read the framework or see the research status when you want the technical distinctions.
